A photorealistic operational documentary photograph inside the active driving cab of a commuter train in autumn. One original adult fictional woman rail driver actively drives an autumn commuter train under low-adhesion leaf-fall restrictions. Her professional rail-driver uniform is visibly tied to operating the train: a tailored dark navy jacket over a pale collared shirt, a neat dark tie, and functional shoulder epaulettes. Seated at the driver's console, she grips the traction-and-brake controller with one hand while the other is poised beside the vigilance controls; illuminated speed and brake gauges face her. Through the broad windscreen, steel rails, a clear lineside signal, and wet crushed leaves on the railhead establish the route and slippery seasonal condition as she makes a cautious controlled approach. Show her alert gaze alternating between the instruments and the track, with upright working posture. Her visible facial structure and long dark softly waved hair are guided only by the supplied appearance reference, realizing a new adult fictional person rather than reproducing identity. Use a three-quarter medium-wide cab view, natural overcast daylight, practical instrument glow, realistic fabric and worn control surfaces, and enough depth to keep both her operational action and the forward railway context unmistakable.
